title: Using Table Partitioning and Data Compression

facts.text: Table partitioning divides large tables across filegroups for faster maintenance, improved queries, and better performance via partition elimination.
Partitioning field must be included in the table's primary key in AL code; partitioning is configured in SQL Server after table publication.
Primary key fields cannot be added after an extension publishes to production; partitioning is limited to new extensions or existing ones with partitioning fields already in primary keys.
Compression reduces table size and improves I/O-intensive workload performance; CompressionType property lets you set Row, Page, or Unspecified compression.
In Business Central online, tables are compressed using Page compression by default.
Partitioning and compression can be combined for flexible data archiving on historical partitions without CPU overhead on active parts.
